messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — we should standardize the reranking response to make score semantics explicit. Proposal: add a small schema change + routing hint so callers can opt into higher-precision scoring and model fanout. Backcompat default: legacy `score` float preserved.
priya: +1 to explicit semantics. What do you mean by "higher-precision"? 32-bit float vs quantized? also how does this affect quota/cost accounting?
alex: By "precision" I mean two orthogonal things: numeric precision (float32 vs float16/quantized) and score interpretation (raw logit, calibrated probability, normalized rank score). Need to label which one in the response so downstream consumers don't misinterpret.
jamie: We should also think about server-side routing. If a request opts into "precision: high" we may need to route to a different model variant (larger or non-quantized). That has cost + quota implications.
sam: Product note — large customers will want simple toggles. Prefer an opt-in param on the endpoint rather than silently changing payload. Also console needs to show per-route "score mode" and expected cost delta.
maya: Draft response example — keep legacy shape but add a stable "score_meta":

```json
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "c1",
      "text": "...",
      "score": 3.142,
      "score_meta": {
        "mode": "raw_logit",        // raw model logit
        "numeric_format": "float32",
        "model": "r-rank-1a",
        "affinity": "primary",
        "fallbacks": ["r-rank-1b"]
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_version": "v2-score-meta"
}
```

maya: Also suggest a cheaper "score_units" concept returned per-response for visibility: e.g. `{"score_units": 12}` where units = sum(candidates * per-candidate cost factor) so billing and telemetry line up.
priya: Telemetry-wise we should emit metrics: `rerank.score_mode`, `rerank.score_units`, `rerank.model_affinity` and histograms for score distributions per-mode. That helps detect regressions when rolling out new modes.
jamie: For quota enforcement, we can translate `score_units` to existing token/quota system. Implementation plan: compute units at admission control and tag request with `x-score-units`. If over quota, reject with 429 and payload telling the caller how many units they'd need.
sam: UX ask — console should show an estimated per-call cost delta when toggling score_mode in the route config. Can we also add a canary toggle (route X% traffic to high-precision)?
alex: yes to canary. Routing policy idea: `model_fanout` param where platform can run N models in parallel for each candidate and emit aggregated score. Default fanout=1. Fanout>1 => higher score_units.
maya: Example of fanout output (simplified):

```json
{
  "id": "c2",
  "text": "...",
  "scores": [
    {"model": "r-rank-1a", "value": 2.9, "type": "raw_logit"},
    {"model": "r-rank-1b", "value": 2.7, "type": "raw_logit"}
  ],
  "aggregate": {"method": "mean", "value": 2.8},
  "score_meta": {"affinity": "primary,ensemble"}
}
```

priya: Ensemble outputs are useful but double-check privacy/audit surface: multiple models could have different data access rules (private vs hosted). Need to gate fanout by customer tier/region.
jamie: Agreed. We'll forbid cross-privacy fanouts by policy. Also need a rollout gate: default v1 route continues to emit `score` only. New `response_version=v2-score-meta` opt-in. Console will expose migration checklist.
sam: OK — deliverables: RFC + migration doc (callers, examples), console change (route toggle + cost estimator), telemetry to infra, and enforcement hooks for quota and privacy. Priority P1 for next sprint because enterprise customers requested explicit semantics.
alex: I'll write the RFC. Quick questions to resolve in RFC: (1) canonical score types to support (raw_logit, probability, normalized_rank), (2) unit formula for `score_units` (suggest: ceil(sum(models_used * candidate_count * model_weight))), (3) default aggregate methods and representation.
maya: I'll prototype server-side headers: `X-Score-Units: 12` + `X-Response-Version: v2-score-meta` and a small parser in the SDKs to keep older SDKs backward compatible.
deploy-bot: canary deploy r-rerank-service v1.8.0 -> eng-platform-canary started 1932109950, 3 nodes. Logs available: https://deploys.internal/r-rerank/1932109950
jamie: Great — once RFC is up ping infra@ so they can scope quota changes. Also want a short runbook for 429s when users exceed score_units.
priya: One more thing — evals. Before enabling normalized probabilities by default we need A/B on downstream ranking metrics (NDCG/CTR) and a regression alert in Optimize.
alex: All noted. I'll drop the RFC by EOD and attach a small migration checklist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
